COURT'S OR JUDGE'S ORDERS
WPSS/2263/2022
Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J
1. Mr. Shivanand Bhatt, learned
counsel for the petitioner.
2. Mr. G.S. Negi, learned Additional
C.S.C. for the State of Uttarakhand.
3. Petitioner was offered appointment
on compassionate ground as Clerk in
Department of Ayurvedic and Unani
Services, Uttarakhand in the year 2011.
In this writ petition, he has challenged
order dated 15.10.2022 passed by
Director, Ayurvedic and Unani Services,
whereby direction was issued to relieve
six ministerial employees, who were
appointed against supernumerary posts,
for Watershed Department.
4. Petitioner contends that he was not
heard before passing the relieving order
and juniors to him are retained in
Department of Ayurvedic and Unani
Services.
5. Learned State Counsel, however,
submits that petitioner's father was a
Group 'D' employee, who died in harness
and petitioner was given compassionate
appointment on a Group 'C'
supernumerary post, as there was no
vacancy available on the post of Junior
Clerk. He submits that petitioner is a
surplus employee in the Department of
Ayurvedic and Unani Services, while
there are other State Departments,
where there is shortage of ministerial
employees. He submits that State

2026:UHC:4284
Government took a policy decision to
shift surplus employees, appointed
against supernumerary posts, to other
Departments, where there was need of
ministerial employees, and pursuant to
that decision, petitioner was relieved for
Watershed Department. He points out
that Watershed Department had also
given consent for petitioner's transfer
and petitioner is now serving in
Watershed Department at Dehradun.
6. This Court do not find any reason to
interfere with the relieving order, as
petitioner has been relieved pursuant to
a policy decision taken by State
Government. It is in dispute that
petitioner was appointed against a
supernumerary post. Since he is surplus
in Department of Ayurvedic and Unani
Services, therefore, State Government
can very well utilise his services in some
other Department where there is dearth
of ministerial employee.
7. The purpose of compassionate
appointment is to provide immediate
financial help to the family of the
deceased employee. In the present case,
petitioner's father was a Group 'D'
employee, yet petitioner was given
appointment on a Group 'C' post, which
is higher in status; that status has
remained unchanged and he is now
serving in Watershed Department on a
Group 'C' post. Thus, there is no
prejudice caused to petitioner by his
transfer and his conditions of service also
remain unchanged. In such view of the
matter, this Court do not find any reason
to interfere with the relieving order.
8. Learned counsel for the petitioner
then submits that some persons, who

2026:UHC:4284
were appointed after the petitioner on
compassionate ground, have been
retained in Department of Ayurvedic and
Unani Services.
9. If that is so, the writ petition is
disposed of with liberty to petitioner to
make representation to Director,
Ayurvedic and Unani Services. If such
representation is made within ten days
from today, decision thereupon shall be
taken, as per law, within four months
thereafter.
 (Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J)
